notes.subject: WIN-013 / WIN-014 verdict reframe to Refuted by Data — anchor on κ as dome's structural mechanism, demote self-contradiction to defense neutralization. Keep it simple.
notes.body:
## What I want

Reframe WIN-013 (currently Misleading) and WIN-014 (currently Self-Contradicted) to **Refuted by Data**. The taxonomy already has this tier (9 wins). No new tier needed.

## Why the reframe — structural argument

The current writeups bury the strongest argument under unfalsifiability framing. The strongest argument is empirical, not methodological:

1. The dome has established **κ = 1.67 nT/µGal** as a coupling constant — a structural model parameter that says "wherever you see a magnetic anomaly ΔB during an eclipse, you should see ΔB/κ as a gravity anomaly at C1/C4 contact phases." κ is referenced in WIN-012, WIN-014's current detail text, monitor.py Domain #7, and PRED-TIER-3's derivation. The dome **needs κ to be real** for PRED-TIER-3 to compute — they literally divide PRED-TIER-1 (predicted ΔB for August 2026) by κ to produce the 10–13 µGal target.

2. If κ is a real coupling, it does not get to skip past eclipses. The 1999 (Membach) and 2009 (China network) eclipses had measurable magnetic anomalies at observatories co-located with operating SGs. Through κ, those magnetic anomalies imply predicted gravity pulses of order few µGal at C1/C4 — well above modern SG noise floors (0.01–0.1 µGal).

3. The SGs were continuously sampled across C1/C4. They saw zero.

4. **The dome model's own coupling-constant prediction failed the data.** That is refutation by data, not non-discrimination, not self-contradiction.

This is cleaner than the current verdict text because the burden of proof flips. Old framing said "you can't claim credit for both null and positive without an advance rule" — that's a methodological complaint a defender can engage at the methodology level. New framing says "your own published model output predicted X, the data shows 0, X ≠ 0, refuted" — that's a substantive empirical complaint with no easy escape.

## Where the self-contradiction argument goes

Demote it from primary verdict text to the **defense-neutralization** subsection. Structure:

- **Primary finding (Refuted by Data):** κ × ΔB(1999) ≠ 0; SG(1999) = 0. Same for 2009. The model's prediction failed the historical data.
- **Defense neutralization:** Any retreat the dome can construct — κ doesn't apply to 1999, instrumental noise, Chebychev filter blocked it, mechanism changed between 1999 and 2026, time-dependent κ — every one of those retreats also destroys PRED-TIER-3, because κ is the only published mechanism producing the 10–13 µGal August prediction. Dome is in a vise: κ applies (and 1999/2009 refute it) or κ doesn't apply (and PRED-TIER-3 has no derivation). Either way, one of the wins falls.

## Scope

**Primary scope** (this commission): WIN-013, WIN-014 verdict text rewrite.

**Possible scope expansion** (your call, analyst): 
- **WIN-058b** (Bedrock Induction Ratio κ = 1.677, currently "Not Demonstrated") — the dome claims the same κ value operates in storm contexts (Halloween 2003 G5). If κ is universal, every G-class storm with measurable ΔB at SG-co-located stations should have produced predicted gravity coupling. Many haven't. The same refutation-by-data argument may apply, or you may decide it stays "Not Demonstrated" for different reasons. Your judgement call on whether to fold WIN-058b into this EXP or leave as a follow-up.

**Research notes for follow-up** (do NOT force into this EXP — flag for later if interesting):
- **WIN-010** (BOU 2017 −10.9 nT, Std Model Explains): if κ is real, κ × (−10.9) ≈ −6.5 µGal should have shown up at the SG nearest BOU during the 2017 eclipse. Was a co-located SG operating? If yes and it showed null, that's another κ-refutation data point.
- **WIN-025** (2024 eclipse 9-station magnetic, Std Model Explains): ±10 nT magnetic implies ±6 µGal κ-predicted gravity. Were any 2024 eclipse-path SGs continuously sampled?
- **WIN-068** (39-eclipse magnetic ensemble 1991–2016, Std Model Explains): 207 magnetic measurements. If κ is universal, this is 207 prediction-and-test cases. The structural argument scales — κ should have been refuted long ago by any working SG during any moderate-magnitude eclipse with co-located magnetic anomaly.

These three are not in primary scope because their current verdicts are already adequate (Std Model Explains is correct for what they claim). But they're potential supporting cites: "κ has had multiple opportunities to manifest as predicted gravity coupling at SG instruments during eclipses with documented magnetic anomalies, and has not done so."

## Critical guidance: keep it simple

The existing WIN-013 and WIN-014 detail_evidence is **all over the place**. Lots of facts, little glue. Pages of text covering: instrumental hierarchy, three-way trilemma on EM-vs-gravity-vs-location-dependent, subsurface conductivity escapes, Yang & Wang reanalysis, dielectric boundary transition reframe, Chebychev filter contradiction, magnitude mismatch with PRED-TIER-2, parameter-retention argument, monitor.py self-validation tautology, Exhibit A graph forensics, GRACE L1A unit issues, retconned escape clauses about C1/C4 timing.

Most of that material lives more naturally in **WIN-011 (Mohe quality)** and **WIN-012 (κ derivation)**. WIN-013/14 should focus narrowly on:
- One sentence: dome claims SG null confirms (cite their predictions site).
- Two-three sentences: κ is the dome's structural mechanism for translating magnetic to gravity (cite WIN-012/14/PRED-TIER-3, no need to re-litigate κ's derivation here).
- Two-three sentences: κ × ΔB(1999) gives a few-µGal predicted pulse; SG measured 0; refuted. Same logic for 2009.
- Defense-neutralization subsection: the κ-doesn't-apply escapes all destroy PRED-TIER-3 (cross-reference WIN-014 and PRED-TIER-3, don't re-explain).
- Cross-link to WIN-011 and WIN-012 for κ derivation issues; cross-link to PRED-TIER-3 for forward-prediction stakes.

**Target length per WIN: 1/3 to 1/2 of the current detail_evidence**, not a longer rewrite. The point should land on first read; readers shouldn't have to assemble the argument across paragraphs.

Prune ruthlessly. If a fact doesn't directly support "dome predicted X via κ; data showed 0; refuted," it goes to a different WIN or gets cut.

## Empirical work needed

To make the κ × ΔB computation concrete, please pull:

1. **1999 European eclipse**: ΔB at a magnetometer co-located with or nearest to Membach during August 11 1999 totality. INTERMAGNET archives have this. We need a defensible number to multiply through κ.
2. **2009 East Asia eclipse**: ΔB at magnetometers co-located with the China SG network during July 22 2009. Same drill.

If the published 1999 magnetic-anomaly value at Membach-co-located observatories yields, say, ~3 nT, then κ × 3 ≈ 1.8 µGal — well above Membach SG's ~0.01–0.1 µGal noise floor. Document the actual values. Don't make them up; if you can't find a clean cite, say so and use "of order few nT" framing rather than fabricating precision.

## Pipeline

Standard analyst Mode 2/2b: write EXP-NNN with rewritten detail_evidence + detail_verdict_text for WIN-013 and WIN-014 (and possibly WIN-058b if you decide to fold it in). Curmudgeon reviews under standard rubric. Decider integrates after curmudgeon clears.

Operator (me) wants to **read the rewritten verdicts before curmudgeon clears** — please make the EXP a single integrated proposal so I can review the analyst draft in one sitting, not split across multiple smaller EXPs.

## References

- ISS-1870 (the original verdict-upgrade issue) — see open-issues.json
- WIN-011 detail_evidence — current Mohe quality writeup, where the WIN-011 nuance arguments belong
- WIN-012 detail_evidence — current κ derivation writeup, where the κ circularity arguments belong
- PRED-TIER-3 in data/predictions.json — the forward prediction the κ-doesn't-apply escapes destroy
- monitor.py Domain #7 — the κ hardcoded-identity-check code (cite once for the mechanism, don't re-litigate the circularity)

---

## Addendum 1 (2026-05-09T20:40:35Z) — Create a κ-Cluster section, parallel to MOND grouping

Following the same structural pattern as the MOND grouping section: the individual WIN entries can stay terse only if the structural argument lives in one place that they cross-reference. Without this, every WIN in the κ-cluster would have to re-litigate the coupling-constant logic to make its point land. With it, each WIN cites the section and stays focused on its specific empirical fact.

### Section commission

Create a new section in the review titled **"The κ Coupling Cluster"** (working title — analyst may refine, but match the simplicity of "The MOND Grouping" naming style). Place it in **Section 6** alongside the MOND grouping unless analyst sees a strong reason to put it elsewhere. (Other live options: Section 7 if 6 is filling up; sub-tab on the eclipse predictions page if we want the dome author to find it more readily. Default to Section 6.)

### Section structure (8 parts — analyst may merge or reorder)

1. **What κ is and why it's load-bearing.** The dome has elevated a one-shot ratio (Mohe 1997 µGal ÷ BOU 2017 nT) into a structural model parameter. Cite where it appears: WIN-012 (definition), WIN-014 (explicit reference), monitor.py Domain #7 (hardcoded constant), PRED-TIER-3 (forward derivation). Establish that without κ there is no published mechanism producing 10–13 µGal as a predicted target — this is the reason the dome cannot drop κ.

2. **How it was derived.** κ = -10.9 nT (BOU magnetometer, 2017 US eclipse) ÷ -6.5 µGal (Mohe spring gravimeter, 1997 China eclipse) = 1.677. Two eclipses, two continents, two decades, two instrument types. No co-located simultaneous measurement of both quantities at any single eclipse. (Brief — the derivation-circularity arguments live in WIN-012; this section just establishes the cross-eclipse cross-instrument origin.)

3. **What κ predicts in past eclipses.** Both 1999 (European, Membach SG) and 2009 (East Asia, China SG network) had documented magnetic anomalies at observatories co-located with operating SGs. Through κ, those magnetic anomalies imply gravity pulses of order few µGal at C1/C4 — well above modern SG noise floors of 0.01–0.1 µGal. Use the actual ΔB values you pull for the empirical work above; don't fabricate.

4. **What past SG data actually shows.** Zero. Continuously sampled across contact phases. No anomaly above noise floor. Cite Van Camp 2001 and the 2009 China network publications.

5. **The vise.** Either κ applies generally (and 1999/2009 refute it as published) or κ has unspecified scope restrictions (and PRED-TIER-3 has no derivation). No third option appears in the dome's published material. This is where the demoted self-contradiction argument from the WIN-013/14 verdicts lives — the section is its proper home.

6. **The storm corollary (WIN-058b).** Same κ value claimed in Halloween 2003 G5 storm context. Same vise applies — if κ is universal, every G-class storm with co-located ΔB and SG should have produced predicted coupling. Many haven't. Brief subsection; WIN-058b cross-references it.

7. **What the dome could do.** Publish scope conditions for κ with timestamps independent of the data. Until that happens, the carve-outs the dome periodically deploys (Chebychev filter, instrumental noise, mechanism change between 1999 and 2026, dielectric vs. shielding interpretations) read as post-hoc retreats designed to absorb whichever data point is currently inconvenient. Tie back to the canary / OTS framework — this is exactly the kind of post-hoc carve-out that timestamping prediction documents independently of observation documents would prevent.

8. **WIN cluster cross-reference table.** Inline summary linking the section to: WIN-010 (numerator), WIN-011 (denominator), WIN-012 (definition), WIN-013 (1999 refutation case), WIN-014 (2009 refutation case), WIN-058b (storm corollary), WIN-025 (2024 eclipse — research candidate), WIN-068 (39-eclipse ensemble — research candidate), PRED-TIER-1 (forward magnetic), PRED-TIER-2/3 (forward gravity).

### How individual WIN entries should change in the same EXP

With the section in place, each WIN's detail_evidence shrinks substantially:

- **WIN-013:** "The dome claims the Membach SG null confirms the model. Refuted by data: applying the dome's own coupling constant κ to the documented magnetic anomaly at Membach-co-located observatories during the August 1999 eclipse implies a predicted gravity pulse of [SPECIFIC VALUE FROM EMPIRICAL WORK] µGal at C1/C4, well above the SG noise floor of 0.01–0.1 µGal. The instrument recorded zero. The model's own published prediction failed the data. See [κ-cluster section] for the structural argument and defense neutralization. (Two more sentences on Membach-specific details — Van Camp 2001 cite, vault description, etc.)" That's the full WIN. ~5–7 sentences total.
- **WIN-014:** Same structure for 2009 China network. ~5–7 sentences total.
- **WIN-012:** Light edits — the κ derivation walkthrough moves to the section (with a back-reference). The self-contradiction-with-WIN-013/14 argument also moves to the section's vise subsection. WIN-012 keeps its Mohe-quality and circular-validation arguments but loses the structural-mechanism scaffolding.
- **WIN-011:** Minimal edits — Mohe spring-gravimeter quality argument is its own empirical claim and stays in WIN-011's text.
- **WIN-058b:** "The dome claims the same κ = 1.677 coupling operates in storm contexts (Halloween 2003 G5). See [κ-cluster section, storm corollary subsection]." Plus 2–3 sentences on the storm-specific empirical claim. ~4–5 sentences total.

### Discoverability mitigation

The one real cost of section-based structure is that a reader landing directly on WIN-013 doesn't see the section unless they follow the cross-reference. To mitigate:

- Make the WIN-013 / WIN-014 cross-references **prominent** — first sentence, not buried. Something like "This finding is part of the κ-coupling cluster; see [section link] for the structural argument that ties WINs 010–014, 058b, and PRED-TIER-1/2/3 together."
- The κ-cluster section itself should be **self-contained** — readable without prior context, with all numerical claims sourced.
- Section's TOC entry / navigation card should be visible at the top of Section 6 alongside the MOND grouping.

### Pipeline implications

This is still a single integrated EXP — verdict reframe + section creation in one proposal. The operator review I requested above covers both the rewritten verdicts and the new section. Don't split into two EXPs; the verdict reframe is incoherent without the section to point at.

If the section commission feels too large to fold into one EXP for analyst, it's permissible to deliver the section as a standalone EXP first (operator reviews → curmudgeon reviews → decider integrates), and then deliver the WIN-013/14 verdict reframe in a second EXP that references the now-published section. Analyst's call. But avoid sequencing where the WIN reframe lands first and points at a section that doesn't yet exist.

### Why this addendum exists rather than a separate HNOTE

The section creation is the same body of analytical work as the verdict reframe — same WINs, same structural argument, same empirical data needed (ΔB values for 1999 and 2009). Splitting it into a separate HNOTE would create coordination overhead between two related analyst commissions. Single integrated commission, single integrated EXP, single operator review.

notes.subject: EXPERIMENT: Compress WIN-012.detail_evidence from 1888w to ~600w. This is a one-off probe to see what real content compression (not mechanical reformatting) looks like. Result feeds amendment-002 (Categories F/G/H) design before operator approves it.
notes.body:
## Context — why this commission exists

PROP-041 Phase 2 (sloppytoppy-rewrite) shipped 2026-05-16. The first run produced one RW (mechanical sentence-splitting on WIN-010.detail_verdict_text) and four PUNTs surfacing a structural gap: the rewriter's Categories A-E can RESTRUCTURE prose but cannot REDUCE content volume. WIN-010 was rewritten with composite 3.0 → predicted 5.4 — mechanically clears the +1.5 delta gate but STAYS BELOW the acceptable_floor of 7.5. Most of the below-floor surfaces are dominated by length, not understandability, and A-E doesn't fix that.

DIRECTIVE-20260516-005 (PROP-041-amendment-002) just asked tinker to spec Categories F (editorial split) + G (forward-ref preview) + H (link-out for depth). Operator's leaning toward 'yes, we want real content compression' but wants empirical evidence before architectural decision. This HNOTE IS that evidence.

The question this commission answers: when a human-grade analyst is given a real over-target WIN and told to compress it with preservation rules, what comes back? Is the compression viable? Does the argument survive? Is the work shape closer to (a) something Opus could do via a rewriter category, (b) something analyst should do as a recurring mode, or (c) something only a human operator can do?

## The target — WIN-012.detail_evidence

Current state: 1,888 words. Target: detail_evidence target_max=600. Compression ratio: 3.15×.

The surface is a Self-Contradicted verdict on the dome's κ coupling constant (κ = 1.67 × 10⁻¹⁰). The core argument is tight: the dome's own WIN-013/WIN-014 measurements (0.0 µGal eclipse-gravity nulls) put zero in the denominator of κ, so κ is undefined. Plus the numerator is a single Halloween 2003 storm event, not a quiet-day baseline. That core argument should fit in 600 words.

Historical note: HNOTE-OPERATOR-WIN-013-014-VERDICT-REFRAME-001 (consumed by EXP-301, 2026-05-10) said WIN-012 should get 'light edits — the κ derivation walkthrough moves to the section (with a back-reference). The self-contradiction-with-WIN-013/14 argument also moves to the section's vise subsection. WIN-012 keeps its Mohe-quality and circular-validation arguments but loses the structural-mechanism scaffolding.' EXP-301 integrated WIN-013/14 verdict reframes + new Part 6.14 κ-cluster section. WIN-012 is still 1888 words, so either the light edits didn't materialize or they weren't enough.

## The compression task

Draft a compressed version of WIN-012.detail_evidence with the following constraints:

### Word target

~600 words. Hard cap 700. If you genuinely can't compress to 700 and preserve the argument, write what you can and tell me in the EXP rationale how much more you'd need and why.

### Must preserve

- Verdict: Self-Contradicted
- Claim verbatim: "Magnetic-gravity coupling constant is 1.67 × 10⁻¹⁰"
- Load-bearing numbers: −10.9 nT, −6.5 µGal, 1.67 × 10⁻¹⁰, 0.0 µGal nulls (from WIN-013/014), Dst = −383 nT
- Key citations: Van Camp et al. 2001 (Membach 1999), Sun et al. 2010 (China 2009 SG network)
- Cross-WIN references to WIN-013, WIN-014
- Cross-reference to Part 6.14 κ-cluster section (where the structural vise argument lives — your compressed WIN-012 should point there for the cluster-level argument and stay focused on κ's own definition + derivation issues)
- The core 3-step refutation chain: (a) Mohe density anomaly not independently replicated → (b) subsequent eclipses found 0.0 µGal at SGs → (c) zero in the denominator of κ makes κ undefined

### Allowed (and encouraged) to cut

- Secondary elaborations on instrumental hierarchy
- The "Chebyshev filter" defender-rescue paragraph if it's there
- Broad-applicability footnote details (the storm-event-not-baseline argument can shrink to one sentence)
- Yang & Wang reanalysis (if present, it can move to WIN-011 or just get cut)
- Detailed walkthroughs of the dome's live-site WIN-013 entry — a one-sentence summary plus a citation is enough

### Allowed to link out

If a cut detail seems genuinely important (e.g., the κ derivation walkthrough, the Mohe quality concerns), point readers to:
- WIN-011 (Mohe quality)
- Part 6.14 κ-cluster section (structural argument + defense neutralization)
- The underlying research (Van Camp 2001, Sun 2010) for the empirical numbers

A 1-sentence summary + link is the right shape for content that would otherwise add depth but doesn't directly support the core 3-step refutation.

### Audit fields required

In the EXP body, include:

- `original_word_count`: 1888 (or recount and report)
- `compressed_word_count`: actual
- `target_word_count`: 600
- `cuts_summary`: bulleted list of what you cut and (briefly) where the content went (cut entirely / moved to WIN-NNN / linked to underlying research)
- `preservation_audit`: confirms verdict, claim, key numbers, key citations all preserved

## Output shape

Write as a standard EXP-NNN.json under monitor/analyst/expansions/ with these fields:
- `mode`: "compression" (new — flags this as a different shape than normal expansions; tells decider intake to hold for operator review rather than auto-route to curmudgeon)
- Standard EXP fields (id, target_win_id='012', target_field='detail_evidence', proposed_text, rationale, etc.)
- The audit fields above

## Pipeline / HOLD for operator review

**Do NOT route to curmudgeon. Do NOT integrate.** Operator (me) wants to read the compressed prose first. If the compression is viable, we feed it back as evidence for the amendment-002 design conversation, then decide:

- Keep this as one-off analyst-compression-mode (commission via HNOTE when needed)
- Promote to a recurring analyst Mode 6 (or analyst-baby Mode 2)
- Build a separate dome-compressor agent
- Just integrate this one and accept that hand-compression is a manual operator/analyst-as-needed activity

Decider, when you see the EXP with `mode='compression'`, route to HOLD-for-operator-review (not curmudgeon, not integrate). Same pattern as Mode 5 frozen-pred drafts.

## What this experiment will tell us

If the result is clean and the argument is preserved: content compression is viable, the question becomes WHO does it (analyst commission vs new agent vs rewriter category extension).

If the result is poor (argument suffers, key facts dropped, prose feels gutted): content compression is harder than mechanical rewriting, and we should either accept that long WINs are an editorial problem operator handles one at a time, OR find a different intermediate (e.g., 'flag for hand-compression' rather than 'auto-compress').

Either outcome informs amendment-002 design. Tinker is currently authoring amendment-002 and will not finalize before operator review, so this experiment's result will land in time to shape the F/G/H spec.

No urgency. Pick this up at the next analyst run that has spare capacity. Single-WIN, single-field, one-off; should not take a full run by itself.

notes.subject: Fable macro review Commission 1: dome statics (weight / load) writeup. Analyst decides placement.
notes.body:
## Context

The operator commissioned a macro-level review from the new Anthropic 'Fable' model. Output is at /MACRO-REVIEW-PHYSICIST-2026-06-09.md in the repo root (read it directly — it's ~150 lines and worth the full read for context, especially §3 and §5). Fable flagged 7 macro stories we under-cover or miss. Operator has selected three for analyst writeup. The other four (sun energy / day-night-seasons / OPEN-007 moonset as standalone / smaller structural points) are explicitly out of scope for this commission — do not expand. The selection criterion was 'highest-impact, lowest-cost, hardest to defend against'.

## Spot-check caveat (read before writing)

Operator-pre-flight grep against data/sections.json and data/wins.json (before commissioning this work) found Fable's grep verifications were directionally right but technically sloppy on some magnitude claims. Specifically:
- Aether density: Fable claimed 0 hits; actual is 8 qualitative mentions across sections+wins. BUT the SPECIFIC NUMBER 3.4×10¹⁷ kg/m³ and the neutron-star comparison: 0 hits in both files. So the kernel — 'we never quote the number or name what density it is' — is correct.
- Dome statics: Fable claimed 0 hits; actual is 2 qualitative mentions in sections.json, 0 in wins.json. So we have prose around the topic but no quantitative statics argument (no ρgR ~ 10¹¹ Pa kill, no comparison to copper strength).
- One-sentence indictment: Fable's framing 'pieces exist but never assembled as one sentence' is accurate — grep finds 26 piece-mentions, 0 assembled headline.

**Implication for analyst:** before authoring, re-run the same greps against current data files to know the CURRENT coverage baseline. The writeups below should aim to *add the missing quantitative anchor / specific number / assembled headline* — not to repeat ground we already cover. If any of the three turns out on second look to be largely covered, downgrade the scope to 'sharpen existing prose with the missing specific' rather than full new writeup.

## Commission 1 — The Dome Has No Statics (Weight of the Dome)

**Source story:** Fable §3.2. The dome model specifies a cast copper/bronze shell with apex height 8,537 km spanning a 40,030-km disc. A self-supporting shell's compressive stress scales like ρgR. For copper (ρ ≈ 8,960 kg/m³) at the scale of thousands of kilometers, that is of order 10¹¹ Pa — hundreds of gigapascals against copper's ~0.2 GPa yield strength. Off by three orders of magnitude. (Same reason real mountains top out near 10 km — the analogy is lay-accessible and worth keeping.)

**The deeper point** (this is the one that lands hardest): the dome cannot even compute the load on its own shell, because the model has no theory of gravity. The statics question isn't just unanswered — it is unanswerable from inside the model. Structural argument, not a gotcha. Connects to existing §1.7 gravity-paradox material (Q-factor argument analyzes the shell electromagnetically but never asks whether it can exist mechanically).

**Empirical work needed:**
1. Verify the 8,537 km apex / 40,030 km disc / copper-bronze composition claims from john09289.github.io/predictions model page directly — quote source verbatim and OTS-attribute if possible.
2. Verify the compressive-stress arithmetic — ρgR with appropriate g (use Earth-surface 9.8 m/s² as starting baseline; note that the dome model's own g varies but the kill survives at any reasonable g it could publish).
3. Verify copper yield strength ~0.2 GPa from a standard materials reference; cite.
4. Pull the existing two qualitative sections.json mentions and decide whether they get folded into the new writeup or stay separate.

**Placement decision (analyst's call):** options to consider —
- (a) New standalone section under an umbrella 'Questions the Model Never Answers' parent (Fable's R1 framing) — but operator has NOT commissioned the umbrella, so this option may want a smaller container.
- (b) Folded into existing §1.7 gravity-paradox as a quantitative companion (cleanest IF §1.7 has room to expand without becoming a 'comprehensive coverage' bloat).
- (c) New kill-shot row (KS-008?) — appropriate IF the argument cleanly satisfies our kill-shot criteria (binary, falsifiable, low-physics-prerequisite). Fable noted KS-008 is candidate for OPEN-007 moonset, NOT for this. Don't conflate.
- (d) New WIN-NNN entry — likely not, since the dome makes no claim about statics that we'd be refuting. WINs are for his claims.

Operator leaning: probably (b) or (a)-with-small-container. Analyst's call after reading current §1.7 and the surrounding section structure.

**Lay framing target (Fable's suggestion, can be refined):** 'Before asking whether the dome explains the sky, ask whether it can hold up its own roof. The model can't answer — it doesn't have a theory of weight.'

## Commission-wide notes

**Single EXP vs three EXPs:** analyst's call. The three commissions share the 'Fable-review-followup' provenance but are otherwise independent (different sections, different evidence, different placement decisions). Default to three separate EXPs unless there's a strong integration argument. Three lets the operator approve incrementally and decider integrates each as it clears curmudgeon.

**Scope boundary — what NOT to do:**
- Do NOT expand into Fable's other four macro stories (sun energy / day-night-seasons / OPEN-007 as standalone exhibit / smaller structural absences). Those are out of scope for this commission. Operator may commission later but not now.
- Do NOT promote any of these to KS-008 or higher-tier kill-shot designation unless the argument cleanly satisfies our kill-shot criteria. The kill-shots tab has explicit binary-falsifiable criteria; statics and aether-density arguments are structural, not pre-committed binary tests.
- Do NOT rewrite the §1.5 escape-hatch argument from scratch. Aether-density is meant to be a quantitative anchor inside it, not a replacement.

**Operator review:** routes through standard analyst→curmudgeon→decider. Operator (me) is happy to read the EXP drafts before curmudgeon if a major architectural question surfaces (e.g., Commission 1's placement decision); otherwise normal pipeline. No HOLD-for-operator-review required.

**Cross-references:**
- MACRO-REVIEW-PHYSICIST-2026-06-09.md (the Fable review itself)
- Existing §1.5 escape-hatch (target for Commission 2 fold-in)
- Existing §1.7 gravity-paradox (target for Commission 1 fold-in if option b chosen)
- Existing §6.12 (one of the source-pieces for Commission 3)
- Existing Overview tab (primary placement candidate for Commission 3 KPI tile)
- data/predictions.json, data/uncounted-failures.json (Commission 3 live verification)

notes.from: operator (cowork session 2026-07-04) — external Claude review of funwithscience.net/dome-model-review commissioned by operator
notes.target: Two independent authoring tasks from an external Claude review (Sonnet 5 or Opus 4.8; independently reproduced our arithmetic and confirmed our science). Full review archived at monitor/tinker/reports/external-claude-review-2026-07-04.md if you need it, but the two focused briefs below are self-contained.
notes.context: External reviewer independently verified every quantitative claim they tested (Schumann 8.78 Hz supremum, 10.2× H drop vs 0.48% g variation, 40,030 km ≈ 2πR_Earth to 174m, 61.46σ ≈ 62.30σ predicted √n scaling, 0 of 11 discriminating April closures, 1 of 70 WINs derived from dome geometry, parallax rejection table). Their overall assessment: our science is right; recommendations are refinements not corrections. Two tasks below are operator-selected as worth pipeline effort.

sub_tasks.title: Author new expansion: Self-gravitational collapse of the disc (Deep Dive H)
sub_tasks.the_argument: The reviewer identifies a macro-physics argument our Part 2 self-contradictions section never makes: a flat, Earth-mass, 20,000-km-radius body is not a mechanically stable configuration under its own gravity. Elegant internal-consistency form (does NOT require appealing to outside authority): the dome posits a local Sun and local Moon, and both are observably round. Roundness of any large body IS the signature of self-gravity in hydrostatic equilibrium (this is why every large body in the universe is spherical; the roundness threshold for rock is only ~300 km radius, e.g. Mimas at 198 km is already round). If self-gravity operates on the Sun/Moon (as their roundness requires), then it operates on the disc too — and the disc collapses to a sphere. If self-gravity does not operate, the Sun/Moon have no reason to be round. The model cannot have selective self-gravity that rounds the local Sun/Moon it places overhead while sparing the disc beneath. Three supporting quantities: (i) roundness ratio: disc radius 20,015 km is ~67× the ~300 km potato radius; (ii) self-gravitational pressure vs rock strength; (iii) collapse timescale ~15 minutes (free-fall time √(3π/32Gρ) at Earth mean density).
sub_tasks.arithmetic_caveat_flag_this: The reviewer stated "central self-gravitational pressure P_c ≈ 3GM²/(8πR⁴) ≈ 170 GPa vs rock strength ~0.2 GPa = 10³× ratio." That formula is the UNIFORM-DENSITY SPHERE central pressure with R = Earth radius (~6371 km). If you use the disc's own 20,015 km radius in the same sphere formula you get ~1.7 GPa (still ~8× rock strength, so the qualitative argument survives, but the specific factor is not 10³×). Also the sphere formula does not directly apply to a disc geometry. Please DERIVE the disc-geometry pressure correctly (or a defensible equivalent stress measure like the central column self-weight ρgh for a flat slab of Earth mean density and 20,000 km depth) before publishing a specific number. The qualitative kill-shot (rock cannot hold this shape) is unaffected; do not overstate the ratio.
sub_tasks.supporting_paragraph_from_reviewer: Killer framing (theirs, worth preserving): "The dome is round physics wearing a flat costume, and the costume cannot bear its own weight." And the recommended placement: BEFORE our current §2.3 gravity-formula critique, because it reframes the debate — before we ask whether the dome's gravity formula is borrowed, we should ask whether the dome as an object can exist.
sub_tasks.secondary_arithmetic: Reviewer also flags a rotating-firmament hoop-stress argument: if the firmament rotates once per sidereal day (standard mechanism for observed diurnal star motion) and is a rigid copper shell as the dome asserts, rim speed at 20,015 km = 1.46 km/s, copper hoop stress σ = ρv² ≈ 19 GPa vs copper yield strength ~0.07 GPa (270× yield). At 50,000 km outer extent σ ≈ 119 GPa (1,700×). This is CONDITIONAL on the dome asserting rotating firmament (its "cast copper/bronze" language implies it). Optional — include as a secondary point if you find it defensible; the self-gravity argument in the main body is unconditional and stronger on its own.
sub_tasks.requested_deliverable: EXP-NNN.json under monitor/analyst/expansions/ proposing a new section titled "Structural Impossibility" (or similar) to be placed at the top of Part 2 (or as a new Part 2.0 preceding §2.1). Content: (a) the self-gravity kill-shot, (b) correctly-derived arithmetic for the disc geometry, (c) the internal-consistency dilemma (round Sun/Moon vs flat disc), (d) optional rotating-firmament secondary. Cite peer-reviewed hydrostatic-equilibrium sources for the roundness threshold (e.g. Lineweaver & Norman 2010 on planetary shape). Standard curmudgeon review + decider integration flow follows.
sub_tasks.not_in_scope: Do not attempt to fold in Deep Dives A–G or the reviewer's presentational recommendations — those are handled by sub-task B or routed elsewhere. Stay focused on this one new content addition.

sub_tasks.title: Three targeted content strengthenings in existing sections

edits.change: Lead the section with what the reviewer calls the invalid-null argument. Currently our critique foregrounds independence violation (√n scaling, shared constants); the invalid-null point sits as a subordinate observation. The reviewer's framing: p = error%/100 is not Uniform(0,1) under H₀. Their empirical check: draw a physical quantity + independent random guess from same population → relative-error distribution has mean ~67%, median ~45%, KS test D=0.16 against Uniform(0,1) rejects at p≈0. Consequence: each dashboard input is a small number not because the null is violated by real signal but because the transform is miscalibrated. This voids the σ INDEPENDENTLY of the independence and counting critiques. Reorder Part 4.1 so this is the LEAD argument, with independence + counting as the reinforcing (also disqualifying) follow-ups.

edits.section: Model tab critique (currently in Part 2 / §2.10 and adjacent)
edits.change: Name a specific invariant explicitly: "no radial-only model can be rescued by refining the radial profile." A 1-D radial function H(r) cannot encode 2-D longitude-dependent structure, in any version. The dome has 13 versions and each has refined the radial profile; none has escaped the dimensionality trap. State this as a named principle so it survives future dome version bumps — every subsequent V51.2 / V52 / etc. refinement of H(r) is answered by pointing at the invariant.

edits.section: Top of site — Part 2 headline slot
edits.change: Lift §2.1 (Schumann supremum) and §2.10 (axial symmetry) to a prominent headline slot at the top of the whole review. Reviewer's note: these are the two strongest and most self-contained arguments (Schumann: dome's own H(r) has hard ceiling 8,537 km → cannot produce 7.83 Hz observed frequency, arithmetic-only, no outside authority needed. Axial symmetry: dome's field equations depend only on r → cannot produce SAA's observed two-lobe longitude structure, math-only, no outside authority needed). Currently at positions 1 and 10 of a 16-item list; they earn front-page real estate.

sub_tasks.requested_deliverable: Three separate EXP-NNN.json files under monitor/analyst/expansions/ (one per edit), each proposing the specific text change + placement + rationale. Small edits, not new sections — but each gets independent curmudgeon review.
sub_tasks.not_in_scope: Do not attempt to add tone-neutralizing edits ("escape hatch" → "post-hoc absorbable correction" etc.) — operator did not select the defensive-polish workstream this round. Stay focused on these three specific strengthenings.
